newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: SK Telecom preferred by foreigners.
newsitem.headline: SK Telecom preferred by foreigners.

text.p: SK Telecom Co was most preferred by foreign investors during pre-opening bidding when the foreign shareholding limit was increased on Friday, the Korea Stock Exchange said.

The bid to share ratio for SK Telecom, the nation's largest cellular phone operator, was 118, the exchange said in a statement issued during mid-morning trade. A total of 11 companies were overbid, it said.

The limit on aggregate foreign ownership in most listed stocks was raised to 23 percent from 20 percent. The limit for Korea Electric Power Corp (KEPCO) and Pohang Iron and Steel Co (POSCO) rose to 18 percent from 15 percent.
The government applies stricter foreign ownership rules to KEPCO and POSCO, which have been designated strategically important companies. KEPCO was not overbid on Friday.
The ratio for steelmaker POSCO was 100.2 times and ranked second in the pre-opening bidding, while the ratio for chipmaker Samsung Electronics Co was 75.2.
The exchange statement said these were the results of bids received from 7:00-8:00 a.m. (2200-2300 GMT Thursday). Thursday was a market holiday. Trading started at 9:30 a.m. (0030 GMT) on Friday.
Among the nine other overbid companies were Kookmin Bank and Shinhan Bank, it added.
